Yes. The **vertical stack** carousel demo is in that repo. It lives here:

**File:**  
`appendix/css-web-ui-demos/carousels-gallery/src/pages/vertical/stack.astro`

So the path is **carousels-gallery → vertical → stack**, not a folder literally named `carousel/vertical/stack/`. In the carousels-gallery Astro app it’s the **Vertical Stack** page under the vertical demos.

It implements:

- **Vertical Stack** – vertical scroll that stacks cards (news-style items from CNN, BBC, NYT, etc.).
- **Scroll-driven animation** – `animation-timeline: view()` and a `stack` keyframe so cards move and scale as they enter/exit.
- **Scroll-state queries** – `container-type: scroll-state` and `@container scroll-state(stuck: top)` to style the “stuck” card (e.g. link color).
- **Scroll buttons** – `::scroll-button(up)` and `::scroll-button(down)` for up/down navigation.

When you run the carousels-gallery app, the route is typically **`/vertical/stack`** (or similar, depending on base URL).

Yes. The **horizontal 3D** carousel from [chrome.dev/carousel/horizontal/3d/](https://chrome.dev/carousel/horizontal/3d/) is in your repo here:

**File:**  
`appendix/css-web-ui-demos/carousels-gallery/src/pages/horizontal/3d.astro`

So the URL path `horizontal/3d/` corresponds to **carousels-gallery → horizontal → 3d.astro**.

This demo does the following:

- **3D carousel** – horizontal scroll with `perspective` and `transform-style: preserve-3d` so cards rotate in 3D (rotateY) as they scroll.
- **Scroll-driven animation** – `animation-timeline: view(x)` and a `carousel` keyframe so each card goes from rotated/back → front → rotated the other way.
- **Scroll buttons** – `::scroll-button(left)` and `::scroll-button(right)`.
- **Scroll markers** – `carousel--scroll-markers` for the dot markers (1–16).
- **Scroll initial target** – 4th slide has `scroll-initial-target: nearest` so it can start in view.
- **Scroll-state** – `@container scroll-state(snapped: inline)` to highlight and scale the centered card (link color, scale 1.75).

The chrome.dev site is the hosted version of this same **carousels-gallery** project; your local copy is the source. Run the carousels-gallery app (e.g. `npm run dev` in `carousels-gallery/`) and open `/horizontal/3d` to see it locally.
